statement: Flavoxat | In lists: 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: May decrease urinary flow, leading to urinary retention | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E || Oxybutynine (non-sustained-release) | In lists: 1, 3, 4, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Anticholinergic side effects (e.g. constipation, dry mouth, CNS side effects); ECG changes (prolonged QT) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Start immediate-release oxybutynin chloride in frail older adults with 2.5 mg orally 2 or 3 times daily. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E || Oxybutynine (sustained-release) | In lists: 1, 3, 4, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Anticholinergic side effects (e.g. constipation, dry mouth, CNS side effects); ECG changes (prolonged QT) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E || Tolterodine (non-sustained-release) | In lists: 1, 3, 4, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Anticholinergic side effects (e.g. constipation, dry mouth, CNS side effects); ECG changes (prolonged QT) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: 1 mg orally twice daily in cases of significantly impaired renal function. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E || Tolterodine (sustained-release) | In lists: 1, 3, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Anticholinergic side effects (e.g. constipation, dry mouth, CNS side effects); ECG changes (prolonged QT) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Use 2 mg orally once daily in cases of severe renal failure (CrCl 10-30 mL/min); avoid use if CrCl <10 mL/min. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E || Solifenacin | In lists: 1, 3, 4, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Anticholinergic side effects (e.g. constipation, dry mouth, CNS side effects); ECG changes (prolonged QT) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Dose reduction may be needed. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E || Trospium | In lists: 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Anticholinergic side effects (e.g. constipation, dry mouth, CNS side effects) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: CrCl <30 mL/min: 20 mg/d (immediate release); avoid the use of extended release trospium. M In adults aged ≥75 years old, the dose frequency of trospium immediate release may be reduced to 20 mg/d. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E || Darifenacin | In lists: 3, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Higher incidence of antimuscarinic adverse events (e.g., dry mouth, constipation, dyspepsia, increased residual urine, dizziness) and urinary tract infection in persons aged 75 years and older compared with younger patients | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E || Fesoterodin | In lists: 3, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Higher incidence of antimuscarinic adverse events (e.g., dry mouth, constipation, dyspepsia, increased residual urine, dizziness) and urinary tract infection in persons aged 75 years and older compared with younger patients | Dose adjustment/special considerations: CrCl <30 mL/min: maximum dose 4 mg/d. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment (pelvic floor exercises, physical and behavioural therapy). E

preambles.text: The aim of the study was to develop a European list of potentially inappropriate medications (PIM) for older people, which can be used for the analysis and comparison of prescribing patterns across European countries and for clinical practice.

preambles.scope: EU(7)-PIM article: dose and alternative suggestions
preambles.text: The PIM list contains suggestions for dose adjustments and therapeutic alternatives. Dose adjustments and drug alternatives suggested by the experts during the Delphi survey were compiled and included in the EU(7)-PIM list, prioritising in each case those made by the higher number of experts. Suggestions were complemented, if necessary, with information available from the other PIM lists and from Micromedex® [[32](http://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4464049/#CR32)], a commercially available database which contains comprehensive information on drug use.

footnotes_and_definitions.text: E: Experts; M: Micromedex ® [32]; P: PRISCUS list [22]; L: Laroche et al (2007) [3]; McL: McLeod et al (1997) [26]; B: Beers list (2012) [18].
Note: if nothing is stated under “Dose adjustment / special considerations of use”, this means that no suggestion was made either by the experts or in Micromedex® .

'In lists' gives the numbered prior PIM lists in which the substance appears, with Category A (precisely this active substance is named as a PIM) or Category B (a PIM only in certain clinical conditions or comorbidities, or not named but covered as a PIM drug class). 'Does not appear as PIM' means the substance was not a PIM in those prior lists; it is still an entry of the EU(7)-PIM list and is not an exclusion. Entries the panel judged questionable carry footnote d.
footnotes_and_definitions.source: EU(7)-PIM ESM1 legend (footnotes a and d)
